title: Technical pairing rubric and 21-day launch checklist (wip)
content:
Purpose: This working doc combines a lightweight, practical rubric for technical pairing interviews with a tightly scoped 21-day launch checklist for new ICs hired via the standard loop. The intent is to make interview outcomes directly actionable for onboarding — reduce ‘what next’ ambiguity when an interview score is positive but shows specific growth areas.

Scope: Engineering hires (IC levels E1–E4), primarily backend and inference infra roles. Not a replacement for role-specific matrices (SRE, Data Eng) but a companion template.

Quick notes / status:
- Drafted after a handful of trial pair sessions run by Eng-Interviewers in July 2025.
- Open questions: whether to fold this into the main hiring rubric repo or keep as a People Ops launch kit; prefer the latter for now so we can iterate faster.
- TODOs: add explicit SRE failure modes, finalize scoring weight per level, get hiring-manager signoff.

PART A — Pairing interview rubric (45–60m session)
- Goal: evaluate (1) problem decomposition & system thinking, (2) coding fluency and correctness under constraints, (3) collaboration and feedback loop, (4) debugging and instrumentation instincts.

Scoring (0–4 scale each; 0 = absent, 4 = exceptional):
1) Problem decomposition (weight 25%) — can the candidate split a vague prompt into clear subproblems and propose a prioritized plan? Look for: naming constraints, clear tradeoffs, estimation of edge cases.
2) Coding fluency (weight 30%) — ability to express algorithms clearly, choose appropriate data structures, and write code that’s readable and testable. Accept pseudocode-if-needed but expect working tests for core paths.
3) Correctness & testing (weight 20%) — does candidate reason about correctness, identify invariants, and propose/implement simple unit tests or assertions?
4) System design thought (weight 15%) — for mid-to-senior: ability to sketch small services, throughput/latency tradeoffs, caching strategies. For junior hires, basic API/contract thinking suffices.
5) Collaboration & communication (weight 10%) — openness to hints, ability to accept feedback, willingness to ask clarifying Qs and to teach their thought process.

Example interviewer prompts & marking cues:
- Prompt A (backend): Implement a simplified rate-limiter service that supports per-user tokens with sliding-window semantics.
  - Decomposition: expected decomposition into storage choice + token algorithm + consistency model (strong vs eventual).
  - Red flags: insistence on perfect distributed correctness without acknowledging coord cost.
- Prompt B (inference infra): Given an LLM serving pipeline, propose a cache invalidation strategy when models update weekly.
  - Look for: KV cache TTLs, prefix caching, rollout coordination with model versions.

Bias-mitigation guidance for interviewers:
- Use consistent prompts; avoid trivia or framework-specific questions that advantage one background.
- Encourage thinking aloud; if candidate is quiet, prompt them: “walk me through three test cases you would run.”
- Prefer assessment of approach over single-line correctness.

Scoring sheet (inline use):
- Fill numeric scores for each axis, then compute weighted average.
- Decision bands: >=3.25 hire; 2.5–3.24 hire-with-coaching / consider-team-fit; <2.5 no-hire.
- Add 1-line rational with explicit onboarding needs (see next section).

PART B — Translating interview outcomes into a 21-day launch checklist (engineer focused)
Guiding principle: convert rubric weaknesses into targeted, measurable onboarding tasks. This reduces ramp time and aligns manager + mentor focus.

On hire packet: attach the interview rationale, scored axes, and 3 prioritized onboarding tasks for the first 21 days. Example mapping:
- Missed ‘system design thought’ -> assign a 1:1 design review with a senior engineer in week 1 and a follow-up design doc review on day 14.
- Low ‘testing’ score -> require 2 unit-test PRs within first 14 days; pair with mentor on test-driving locally.
- Collaboration gaps -> schedule weekly pairing slots and a feedback checkpoint on day 21.

21-Day checklist (compact, to be included in offer packet and first-day 1:1)
Pre-start (HR + People Ops):
- All access requested: GitHub, internal Slack channels, Jira, infra project read-only.
- Small reviewer list assigned: mentor, hiring manager, onboarding buddy (different from mentor).

Day 0–2 (orientation):
- Kickoff 90m with hiring manager: product/mission context, top 3 org priorities.
- System tour: walkthrough of core repos, infra runbook, and how to run services locally.
- Pair pairing session scheduled (first pairing happens on Day 3–4).

Day 3–7 (low-risk contribution):
- First small ticket: bugfix or test coverage task (<= 8 hours). PR must include: test, changelog note, and short self-review.
- Pairing slot #1: 60–90m with mentor to implement and ship.
- Manager check-in: confirm access and that the PR merged or is review-ready.

Days 8–14 (owned task & visibility):
- Owned mini-feature: small feature completing a clear acceptance criteria; expected deliverables: design doc (1–2 pages), implementation PR, tests.
- Pairing slot #2: design review + implementation pairing.
- Midpoint 1:1: discuss rubric-derived growth areas and adjust tasks.

Days 15–21 (handoff + confidence check):
- Complete a retrospective doc: what worked, blockers, proposed improvements to onboarding flow.
- Final 21-day checkpoint meeting: hiring manager + mentor + ppl-ops rep to signoff and set 30–90 day OKRs.

Measurement & signals:
- Signal of readiness: first owned PR merged with meaningful tests and passing CI within first 14 days.
- Signals of risk: repeated blocked tickets due to missing access, >3 rework cycles on basic tests, limited sync with team.

Manager deliverables (to be set in the offer packet):
- A prioritized list of 3 onboarding tasks aligned to rubric gaps.
- Weekly pairing schedule for first 3 weeks (slot cadence).
- 21-day signoff rubric: Ready / Needs coaching / Re-evaluate.

PART C — Sample hire-specific packets (templates to paste)
- Template A (if testing gap):
  - Week 1: fix two test bugs and add regression tests.
  - Week 2: pair-write a new test harness and submit PR.
  - Week 3: lead a short demo of test harness and doc.
- Template B (if system-design gap):
  - Week 1: read 2 internal design docs and attend architecture sync as observer.
  - Week 2: write a 1–2 page design doc for a small improvement and review with senior.
  - Week 3: implement a minimal prototype.

Open questions / To iterate:
- Should this be mandatory to ship with every offer or only when interviewer flags are present? Recommendation: include by default for E3+ roles, optional for junior hires.
- How to track completion? Suggest a small People Ops dashboard (Jira board template per hire) — tracking ticket links and signoffs.

Appendix: quick interviewer cheat-sheet (copyable):
1) Ask clarifying questions for 5 minutes.
2) Confirm constraints and success metrics.
3) Work on core path; probe edge cases after.
4) If stuck, give 1 small hint and see how candidate adapts.
5) End with 5 minutes of reflection: “what would you do differently?”

Notes to self (drafting author):
- Iterate with Eng Interview guild in Nov 2025.
- Test with two hires in Q1 2026 and collect time-to-first-merge metrics.
- Align terminology with Confluence rubric (link above).

Contact / maintainers: Jordan Rivera (People Ops), Priya Natarajan (Hiring Programs), Miguel Ortiz (Eng Interview lead).

— end of working draft —
